ir.name: stable_weighted_logsigmoid_pairwise_normed_diff
ir.intuition: To fix the failure of having empty 'operators_used', this revision explicitly uses standard numerical stabilization and clamping to ensure all operators are recognized and included. The loss computes a normalized pairwise difference of log probabilities scaled by advantage_gap norm with epsilon to avoid division by zero, then applies tanh for smooth normalization. Clamping the scaled difference to [-20, 20] avoids numerical instability in logsigmoid. Weighting the loss and normalizing by sum of weights with epsilon ensures stable aggregation. This yields a numerically stable, semantically meaningful pairwise margin loss with proper operator usage.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon = 1e-6
norm_adv = max(norm(advantage_gap), epsilon)
diff = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm_adv
scaled_diff = scale * tanh(diff)
clamped_diff = clamp(scaled_diff, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(clamped_diff)
weighted_loss = loss * weight
return sum(weighted_loss) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    scale = float(extra.get('hyperparams', {}).get('scale', 1.0))
    epsilon = 1e-6
    norm_adv = ops.norm(advantage_gap)
    norm_safe = ops.maximum(norm_adv, epsilon)
    diff = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm_safe)
    smooth_diff = ops.tanh(diff)
    scaled_diff = ops.mul(scale, smooth_diff)
    clamped_diff = ops.clamp(scaled_diff, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(clamped_diff))
    weighted_loss = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_sum = ops.sum(weighted_loss)
    total_weight = ops.sum(weight)
    norm_weighted_loss = ops.div(loss_sum, ops.maximum(total_weight, epsilon))
    return norm_weighted_loss
